- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is trending down.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1-2 days), leading to overshoot in 30d forecast; cap or dampen forecast after spike.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 7-14 day window and adjust downward if sentiment reversal is confirmed.
- In low-sentiment periods, model tends to underestimate mean reversion; add 1-2% buffer to forecast if sentiment remains flat or negative.
- If 30d forecast is >10% above true outcome, check sentiment history for recent positive spikes — likely overfitting; reduce forecast by 5-10% if sentiment is weak or fading.
- If 30d forecast is <10% below true outcome, sentiment may be weak or negative — consider adding 2-5% upward adjustment if sentiment is recovering or neutral.
